T3.4.message: yasya (p28, genitive of possession) has head p30 (mūrtiḥ) only. But it owns every subject of asti (p29) in this clause: tandrā, nidrā, uṣṇam, śītam, deśaḥ, veṣaḥ, mūrtiḥ. words.w22.notes says this too: 'Yasya gathers the list from tiredness to form: whose is no tiredness, no sleep ... no form.' Pointing it only at the last noun under-describes the dependency. Pointing it at the shared verb p29 (asti) would cover the whole list. A human should decide which convention the dataset uses for a possessive genitive shared across several subjects.
T3.4.suggested_fix: Set padas.p28.head to "p29" (asti), keeping role sambandha, or record in a note that yasya goes with each item in the list.
